llm.reply:
The trials retrieved for this query all concern thyroid cancer, not carcinoma not otherwise specified (NOS) as a named condition, so they only partly answer the question [1]. None of the trial titles names NOS carcinoma [2]. The related literature does cover NOS carcinoma as a histological category in breast cancer [9: "not otherwise specified (NOS) carcinoma"].

## Retrieved Thyroid Trials

One study is Radioimmunotherapy With or Without Chemotherapy Plus Peripheral Stem Cell Transplantation in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer [1]. Another is Thalidomide in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer [2]. A third is Irinotecan in Treating Patients With Metastatic or Inoperable Thyroid Cancer [3]. Others are Tanespimycin in Treating Patients With Inoperable Locoregionally Advanced or Metastatic Thyroid Cancer [4] and Suberoylanilide Hydroxamic Acid in Treating Patients With Metastatic and/or Locally Advanced or Locally Recurrent Thyroid Cancer [5].

## Related Records

A MedGen concept titled Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified was also retrieved [7]. The supporting publication is PMID 15365566 [8]. Its title is Prognostic value of morphology and hormone receptor status in breast cancer - a population-based study. [6]

## NOS Carcinoma Prognosis

In this population-based breast cancer cohort, NOS carcinoma had the poorest survival among microscopically confirmed categories [9: "ranged from 66% (95% CI 61-71) for NOS carcinoma to 95% (95% CI 90-100) for special types"]. Morphology remained an independent predictor [9: "Morphology and hormone receptor status were confirmed as significant survival predictors"].

The retrieved trials all concern thyroid cancer rather than a carcinoma coded as not otherwise specified (NOS), so they only partly answer the question. ## Systemic Therapy Trials

A fourth trial is Tanespimycin in Treating Patients With Inoperable Locoregionally Advanced or Metastatic Thyroid Cancer [4]. A fifth trial is Suberoylanilide Hydroxamic Acid in Treating Patients With Metastatic and/or Locally Advanced or Locally Recurrent Thyroid Cancer [5].

## Related NOS Records

A related MedGen concept is Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [7]. A relevant publication is Prognostic value of morphology and hormone receptor status in breast cancer - a population-based study. [6] Its identifier is PMID 15365566 [8].

## NOS Carcinoma Outcomes

That registry study used NOS carcinoma as one morphology category in breast cancer [9: "medullary carcinoma, not otherwise specified (NOS) carcinoma, other carcinoma"]. NOS carcinoma had the lowest survival among the microscopically confirmed categories [9: "ranged from 66% (95% CI 61-71) for NOS carcinoma to 95% (95% CI 90-100) for special types"]. Morphology independently predicted survival [9: "confirmed as significant survival predictors in this population-based study, even after adjusting for age and stage at diagnosis"].
